missionPremise: OPS-24 P-218, per the 2026-09-15 dispatch and mission_p218_selection_and_situs.md: Part A is a FIX -- a search for 48209:97652 rendered a brief titled 'Parcel 97651' and the export panel refused with 'Export target 48209:97651 is not the selected property (48209:97652)'; the serve layer was pre-cleared by the dispatch (each id's direct read returns its own matching apn), so the defect is client-side selection state, and done means the rendered brief's id always equals the requested id AND a disagreeing export target is impossible to construct, not merely refused. Part B is MEASUREMENT ONLY -- per county, how many parcels carry a real situs, none, or a SENTINEL (present but streetless), and whether the gap is random or tracks a population; no write to the situs join or any acquisition path.
completionPredicate: Part A: a unit-level fixture reproduces the exact production error message and is fixed by the new reconciliation guard (done, verified by the test suite); the fix is merged, deployed, and re-verified live against the actual 97651/97652 pair through the real brief and export panel (NOT done -- see falsifier/contradicted below; this is why the lane is closed-partial rather than closed). Part B: a per-county, three-way (real/none/sentinel) count exists, is reconciled against the dispatch's own cited prior figure rather than taken on faith, and the gap is characterised as random or population-tracking with evidence either way (done in full).
scopeBasis: Part A's fix is scoped to the client selection-state seam named by the dispatch (apps/property-explorer/src/lib/subject-store.ts and the card-writing paths in ExplorerMap.tsx) and does not touch the server/serve layer, which the dispatch pre-cleared and this lane independently re-confirmed live for the four Sturgeon Dr ids rather than re-trusting prose. Part B is bounded to measurement: no situs-join code, no acquisition-path code, and no fix was written or proposed as code, per the dispatch's explicit 'do not write to the situs join or any acquisition path.' The out-of-scope P-214 and P-154 live-FAIL findings the shared probe instrument surfaced are reported, not investigated, because they belong to other rows.

partA.rootCause: Two different client-side stores track 'the current parcel' with no reconciliation between them. subjectStore (subject-store.ts), written only by setSubjectByParcelNodeId, is guarded by ONE unified monotonic generation counter and is thoroughly proven never to let a slower, earlier resolve overwrite a later one (subject-store.test.ts). The rendered card (ExplorerMap.tsx's cardNodeId/inspectedRef, which feeds both the brief title and, via activeParcelNodeId = cardNodeId ?? subjectNodeId, the export panel's 'expected' parcel id) is written by inspectInPlace at five independent call sites, each guarded by its OWN ad hoc mechanism (lookupIntentRef for the search path; a direct inspectedRef comparison inside adoptSubject's callback for the click path). I manually traced every one of those five call sites against every interleaving the subjectStore test suite proves safe at the subjectStore layer and found each individually well-guarded against every race I could construct from them alone; I could not reproduce the operator's exact click sequence with certainty from static reading, and I am reporting that honestly rather than asserting a specific trigger I have not verified. What IS certain and independent of the exact trigger: nothing in the architecture reconciles the two stores once any one guard (present, or a future one at a sixth call site) has a gap, so the disagreement, once introduced by any means, persists indefinitely. REJECTED alternative mechanism: a server-side mislabel. Rejected because the dispatch's own pre-check (each id's direct read returns its own matching apn) is inconsistent with the observed pattern (subjectStore correct, card wrong) -- a server mislabel would make both wrong identically, since both derive from the same resolver.resolve(id) call for whichever id it was actually given.
partA.fix: apps/property-explorer/src/lib/card-subject-guard.ts (new): a pure reconcileCardWithSubject() function. ExplorerMap.tsx now subscribes to subjectStore and applies it on every change, calling the existing inspectInPlace to force the rendered card to converge on the subject's parcel id whenever they disagree -- regardless of which call site let them drift apart. This makes the card a PROJECTION of the subject by construction, completing the file's own stated intent ('the card RENDERS the sheet -- it is a projection, not a re-lookup') as an enforced invariant instead of a five-way convention.

Reselect the property and try again.'
fixtureBeforeAndAfter.after: The second describe block proves the fix: reconcileCardWithSubject({inspectedParcelNodeId: '48209:97651', subject: <sealed 48209:97652 sheet>, ...}) returns {parcelNodeId: '48209:97652', card: {apn: '97652', ...}}; re-deriving the export's expected id from the reconciled card, resolveExportTarget('48209:97652') no longer throws. A no-op test confirms the guard does nothing once the card already agrees, and an AMENDMENT-1-compatibility test confirms a null subject never blanks an inspected card.

partB.reconciledAgainstPriorFigure: The dispatch's cited 99.3%/89.9% is SS-W5 (2026-08-18), a looser 'has a street token' predicate than isUsableSitusAddress. That alone explains Hays/Bell/Bexar/Williamson each showing MORE sentinel here (stricter predicate). It does NOT explain Travis, which moves the OPPOSITE direction by 75 points (SS-W5 17.9% real vs this measurement's 93.6%). Traced to source_vintage: Travis is on stratmap25-landparcels_48453_travis_202508 (Aug-2025 edition) while Hays/Bastrop are on the March-2025 ..._202503 edition; all three counties' current rows were ingested in the SAME 2026-09-03 reload (matching P-212's own timestamp for Bastrop exactly). Travis's coverage was already substantially fixed by a full source-vintage upgrade that landed AFTER the SS-W5 sweep -- the dispatch's 'named fix was a per-county JOIN' framing is stale for Travis specifically; Hays and Bastrop's gaps are real and unchanged.

evidence: By county, sentinel rate ranges 0% to 100% (of 249 counties with 1,000+ parcels: 74 above 50%, 38 below 5%, median 35.9%) -- a uniform data-entry error would not produce this spread.

The SENTINEL VALUE'S OWN SHAPE differs systematically by county: Bastrop's sentinels are 96.4% fully blank (', ,'); Hays's are 82.6% 'street name present, house number absent' (e.g. 'STURGEON DR, SAN MARCOS, TX 78666'). Different counties are missing different PARTS of the address, which argues for different, county-specific repairs rather than one join.

The Sturgeon Dr pair itself confirms the pattern: 97651 and 97652 both carry situs_address = 'STURGEON DR, SAN MARCOS, TX 78666' (present, not null) on a real platted geo_id in the same subdivision as their numbered neighbors 97650/97658 -- vacant lots that never had a house number assigned by the county, not missing data.
gapCharacterisation.unrelatedAnomalyFoundAndContained: prop_id='0' is a placeholder/catch-all identity in 204 of 253 counties (616,287 raw rows statewide, 454,349 in Travis alone) whose situs_address sample is OWNER MAILING addresses, not situs ('TAX DEPT MS 68 198 CHAMPION CT , TX'). The per-parcel dedup this measurement uses collapses it to at most 204 of the 13,072,079-parcel denominator (negligible); a naive per-row count would have let it distort Travis's numbers by nearly half a million rows. Not chased further -- named in leave_behind.

falsifier: Pre-registered per the dispatch: (1) fixing only the refusal message hides the detector -- not what happened, export-target.ts is untouched. (2) the brief rendering correctly while the export target stays independently settable leaves them able to diverge -- closed, because the export's expected id is sourced from cardNodeId, which the new subscription now forces to equal subjectStore's id whenever they disagree. (3) Part B counting a present-but-streetless situs as populated reproduces the exact miscount -- avoided by using isUsableSitusAddress (requires a leading house number) rather than a bare non-null check; the 'none' bucket this measurement reports is correspondingly small (0.55% statewide) because it is a genuinely different class from 'sentinel', not a relabeling of the same miscount.
